newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes up, later pares gains.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes up, later pares gains.

text.p: Gold prices reached their highest levels since mid-Januaryon Wednesday as speculators latched on to a buying spree in the platinum group metals (PGMs).
"The PGMs took over the lead this afternoon and gold began to look a bit toppy as soon as it got over $356.00," one dealer said shortly before profit-taking took the metal off its highs.
Gold fixed at $354.75 per ounce up from $353.85 this morning and marking its highest fix since January 28 this year.
At the fix the New York Comex April gold futures contract was up about $1.00 at $357.10 off an intraday high of $358.70.

The move was partially unexpected. Reflective markets were forecast ahead of the over the counter (OTC) option expiry at 1430 GMT followed half an hour later by the beginning of U.S. Federal Reserve Board chairman Alan Greenspan's semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony.
By the time he was speaking, post-option expiry correction to the gold price ensured a Greenspan-induced downturn in the Dow and U.S. bond prices did not show up positively on bullion.
One of the key option levels was the $355.00 February call below which the market had been hovering most of this week since coming off a 3-3/4 year low on February 12.
According to analysis of historical price charts gold would break out from its current tight range if it dipped to $348.00 or advanced to $358.00, one dealer said.
Greenspan's testimony on the U.S.'s economic health was basically upbeat but he again expressed concern over stock market levels and the risk of inflation.
In a December speech the Fed chairman sent stock markets reeling when he noted equity prices' "irrational exuberance".

Dealers said fund buying in platinum and palladium lifted PGM prices this afternoon following comments from union officials and management at Russia's troubled Norilsk mining and metallurgical complex.
The price of both metals hit recent highs at their fixing.
A union official said the complex could be struck on March 15 by workers who are owned wages back to last October. However a management spokesman later said this was premature.
By 1530 both markets had come off earlier highs with platinum indicated at $381.25/$382.25 and palladium at $147.00/$148.00, up $7.00 and $6.50 respectively.
"Any further disruption to Russia's ability to ship PGMs would cause major problems for consumers," a dealer said.
Silver was largely ignored but by 1530 GMT was three cents firmer at $5.23/$5.25. --London newsroom +44 171 542 8058
